messages:
Ava: Quick ask for runtime — marketing is preparing a launch post and we want a tight spot-probe to substantiate the latency claim. Can eng-runtime run a small randomized probe across these variants and drop raw samples + latency percentiles? We only need a fast, repeatable snapshot, not a full bench.

Ava: Requirements: 1) Variants: stable (non-quantized), int8-quant, int4-quant 2) Sample count: 50 randomized prompts per variant 3) Warmup: 10 prefix warmup requests, then measure 4) Seeded RNG (seed=42) so we can reproduce samples 5) Report: median, p95, p99 latency, token-cost, and 10 raw prompt->response examples per variant (include timestamps & trace id)

Ava: Payload shape — minimal user-facing example (please vary user_id per sample):
```json
{"input": "Summarize the following in 2 sentences: <article_text>", "user_id": "user_<rand>", "trace_id": "mkt-spot-5059994321"}
```

Ava: If you can include one example of a failed/timeout request in the artifacts that would be great for transparency.

Diego: Sounds doable. Quick clarifying q's — which exact model names should we call in the cluster? e.g. redwood/santa-13b, redwood/santa-13b-int8, redwood/santa-13b-int4? Also are we allowed to run this on hosted or should we use a Dedicated sandbox?

Ava: Call the hosted variants listed above (those catalog names are correct). Hosted is fine — we want the claim to reflect what users would see. If capacity is a blocker, fall back to a dedicated small pool but note that in the report.

Priya: Timeline? I can queue this today if we get greenlight. Also: acceptance criteria for marketing claim? e.g. median < 120ms or similar?

Sam: Marketing goal: on the sample workload give a credible median <= 120ms for stable (non-quantized) at 1k token max; p99 should be listed but we won't headline it. If stable misses that, we want numbers for the quantized variants so we can pick the right phrasing.

Diego: OK. Few implementation notes: - We'll use the same seed across variants and deterministic prompt list. - Warmup 10 requests with same prefix to populate KV cache. - Measure end-to-end server-side latency (request queued -> last token emitted). - Will annotate whether prefix caching was hit. Also: 50 samples per variant is fine but cost will be ~ 150 runs x avg tokens.

Diego: Example run command we plan to use (replace TOKEN):
```bash
for variant in stable int8 int4; do
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RENDERTOKEN\" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{\"model\": \"redwood/santa-13b-${variant}\", \"input\": \"Summarize the following in 2 sentences: <article_text>\", \"max_tokens\": 200, \"user\": \"mkt-spot\"}' \
  | jq . > out_${variant}_$(date +%s).json
done
```

Ava: Nice. Please include the raw JSON outputs, and a tiny CSV with latency percentiles per variant. Also mark any runs with kv-cache=false.

Priya: We'll also do a quick content-quality check: sample 10 outputs per variant to ensure no obvious regression. Where should we drop artifacts?

Ava: Put everything into /shared/marketing/bench/spotprobe-5059994321.zip or a GCS bucket and paste the link here.

bench-bot: Scheduled job created: job_id=mkt-spot-5059994321-run1, ETA ~ 30m. Will post artifacts when complete. :mechanical_arm:

Diego: Started job. Running warmup now. Noting: one warmup cluster node had a transient GPU preemption; we'll ignore warmup retries but will surface if it affects measured runs.

Diego: First variant (stable) complete — median=135ms, p95=280ms, p99=420ms. Annotating: prefix-cache hit ~ 86%. Uploading raws.

Ava: Hmm median 135ms is higher than our 120ms goal. Can you run the same with a 20-sample short-tail (shorter prompts) to see sensitivity to input length? If that drops median under 120ms we can frame the claim narrower ("on short inputs").

Diego: Sure — spinning a short-input batch (max_tokens=50), 20 samples per variant.

Diego: Short-inputs results: stable median=98ms, p95=210ms, p99=330ms. int8 median=85ms, int4 median=82ms. Uploading new artifacts and a brief note on token distribution.

Priya: I'll run the quick quality check on the uploaded outputs. If content is comparable we can use short-input phrasing.

Priya: Quick note — a couple of int4 outputs had truncated completions on the long prompt set; not huge but worth flagging in the writeup.

Ava: Perfect. Please create a 1-paragraph summary we can paste into the launch doc with the exact caveats (short-inputs vs long-context, seed, sample counts, percentile numbers). Also include the GCS link here.

Diego: Summary draft uploaded and artifacts at gs://redwood-marketing/spotprobe-5059994321.zip. Raw CSV and 10 sample pairs per variant included.

Ava: Thank you! I'll slot the summary into the launch draft and tag the legal/comms review. If anything else comes up we'll ping here. :tada:
